rows.title: Recession is likely in 2024 because companies face a ‘huge shock’ of having to refinance debt at higher interest rates, top strategist warns
rows.standfirst: The easy-money years of the pandemic left corporations with a slew of debt maturing in a new era of higher rates.

rows.title: CEO of Fortune 1000 builder: U.S. housing market bottom should hold, but if it doesn’t this key metric will warn us
rows.standfirst: What’s actually happening in the U.S. housing market, as told by KB Home CEO Jeffrey Mezger.

rows.title: Housing market affordability is so strained that couples want down payment cash rather than a wedding gift
rows.standfirst: This couple added a “first home-fund”—their one and only request—on their wedding registry.

rows.title: Housing market inventory is so scarce that builders will be in the driver’s seat for years to come, says KB Home’s CEO
rows.standfirst: “A chunk of that [inventory] isn’t even livable,” says KB Home CEO Jeffrey Mezger.

rows.title: Fed’s Raphael Bostic says interest rates will stay higher for longer than people think
rows.standfirst: “We’re going to have to keep our rate higher for longer than historically happens,” he says, “because we need to make sure that inflation stays at 2%.”

rows.title: This millennial entrepreneur has launched 3 startups, earns six-figures, and still doesn’t see the point in buying a house right now: ‘this isn’t even worth the money’
rows.standfirst: “I can afford a house, the thing is, I just ran the numbers and realized it wasn’t the right thing to do”

rows.title: The odds of a recession are now just 15% because fading inflation and a strong labor market are changing the equation, Goldman Sachs says
rows.standfirst: Positive inflation and labor data has prompted Goldman Sachs’ chief economist to rethink the probability of a recession in the next 12 months.

rows.title: I coined the term ‘digital divide’ 25 years ago. Biden is providing the funding to bridge it–but one rule could squander this opportunity
rows.standfirst: Grantees will have to front millions of dollars before they receive a dime from Uncle Sam under the Broadband Equity Access and Deployment (BEAD) program.

rows.title: Trailer park owners used big data to price-gouge residents with ‘blatantly inflated’ rents, lawsuit claims
rows.standfirst: A lawsuit accuses 9 management companies and a data provider of conspiring to fix and inflate lot rental prices at more than 150 locations.

rows.title: September is usually a ‘rotten month for stocks.’ Here are 7 things top analyst Ed Yardeni believes could go wrong this time
rows.standfirst: Since 1945, the S&P 500 has dropped 0.73% on average in September compared with a 0.7% gain for the index across all months over the same period.

rows.title: Redfin: San Francisco home sellers are 4 times as likely to sell at a loss
rows.standfirst: “Roughly one of every eight (12.3%) homes that sold in San Francisco during the three months ending July 31 was purchased for less than the seller bought it for.”

rows.title: A tale of 2 housing markets: The red-hot bottom and ice-cold top
rows.standfirst: “Upper price tier” home values are down 10.7% in Seattle, while “lower price tier” homes are down 1.5%.

rows.title: There’s a housing shortage and an office glut. So why are there only 217 U.S. office-to-resi conversion projects in the pipeline?
rows.standfirst: Ongoing office-to-residential conversions are just a “drop in the bucket” of the projects to come, CBRE researchers say.

rows.title: The man who bought the NYSE just made a $11.9 billion bet that he can fast-track your mortgage for far less than you’re paying now
rows.standfirst: ICE’s Jeff Sprecher is crusading to modernize the painfully slow home loan loop that typically takes around two months and costs about $8,000.

rows.title: The housing affordability crisis is a hidden reason your kid doesn’t have a teacher—stunning report shows teachers can only afford 12% of homes near their work
rows.standfirst: Redfin crunched data on 70,000 schools in the 50 biggest metros and found the housing market zooming up and away from the stagnant teacher’s salary.

rows.title: How an early retiree quit a six-figure job to live off $34,000 a year in rental income

rows.title: Saudi Arabia is squeezing the oil market just as consumption surges: ‘The Fed may have to react’
rows.standfirst: “A cut by Saudi Arabia has a lot more clout than purported cuts elsewhere — when they say they will do it, they really mean it.”

rows.title: The FDIC’s 2023 Risk Review shows the surprising resilience of community banks despite inflation and shifting interest rates
rows.standfirst: There is a growing recognition that small banks are better positioned to maintain the trust and loyalty of their borrowers.

rows.title: San Francisco’s ‘real estate apocalypse’ has the attention of billionaire MacKenzie Scott—just look at her latest donation
rows.standfirst: “The time to act is now before the predicted ‘real estate apocalypse’ makes all Bay Area land and housing so astronomically expensive that it is beyond the reach of any social policy intervention.”

rows.title: This Fortune 1000 real estate giant settles antitrust lawsuits for a reported $83.5 million
rows.standfirst: “This settlement is a significant milestone in this case against the National Association of Realtors and the Nation’s four largest real estate brokerages,” Steve Berman, the attorney for the plaintiffs, wrote in a statement shared with Fortune.

rows.title: Housing affordability is so strained that 2 in 5 Gen Zers say they are working side hustles to save for a down payment

rows.title: Surge pricing but for drinking—one of the U.K.’s largest pub owners is hiking prices on evenings and weekends

rows.title: Inflation was so bad last year that real household income tumbled the most in 12 years, causing families severe economic pain

rows.title: $90 Barbie dress helps drive Zara growth in the inflation-hit fashion industry
rows.standfirst: Zara owner Inditex has revealed a sharp rise in profits despite inflationary pressures – thanks in part to a Barbie capsule collection.

rows.title: New Census data shows why Americans hate the economy despite economists telling us to feel good about it

rows.title: Investors are suddenly feeling bullish about the stock market again–but that doesn’t mean you should start shorting it
rows.standfirst: The contrarian in you might be tempted to use the recent spike in investor optimism as a sign to exit or short the stock market. It doesn’t work that way.

rows.title: Retail sales barely budged in August, up just 0.1% from July, as surging gas prices take a bite out of back to school shopping
rows.standfirst: Retail sales rose 0.6% year-over-year in August, compared with a revised 0.5% increase in July, according to the Commerce Department.

rows.title: There was another hot inflation read in August—wholesale prices surging 1.6%
rows.standfirst: Wholesale prices are still rising more slowly than consumer costs, a sign that inflation may continue to cool.

rows.title: Here’s why Americans are racing to repay their federal student loans before they’re even due

rows.title: What if Jerome Powell pulled off a soft landing and nobody noticed? It’s the economy’s Groundhog Day

rows.title: A supermarket chain is shaming suppliers like PepsiCo over ‘shrinkflation’—by labeling examples on shelves

rows.title: The winner of the $2 billion Powerball jackpot has been buying fancy homes around Los Angeles

rows.title: CEO of firm NYC hired in $432M no-bid contract for housing migrants resigns—and admits to lie about A.I. degree

rows.title: A New York state law requiring job ads to disclose salary ranges just went into effect. It matters to remote workers in other states, too

rows.title: House poor is back: ‘the new normal for the foreseeable future’

rows.title: The rental market is softening so fast in some pockets of the country that landlords have no choice but to offer concessions
rows.standfirst: “With vacancies on the rise, some landlords are doling out one-time discounts to attract renters while maintaining high asking rents on paper.”

rows.title: Wall Street’s Dr. Doom is sounding downright sunny as he predicts a ‘short and shallow’ recession or even no recession at all instead of the epic collapse he saw in 2022

rows.title: Howard Dean: ‘At last, Congress proposes drug pricing reform that works’
rows.standfirst: The Patients Before Middlemen Act strikes at the heart of what makes prescription drugs so unaffordable in the U.S., according to Howard Dean.

rows.title: Top analyst Ed Yardeni raises the odds of recession to 25% citing oil prices rising to $94 and a potential repeat of 1970s-style stagflation

rows.title: Housing market affordability is so strained that this Fortune 500 homebuilder is offering a fixed 4.25% mortgage rate in some communities

rows.title: The age of the city has not ended–but its inequality is fueling the backlash against metropolitan elites

rows.title: Zillow once again shifts its 2024 home price forecast. Here’s why

rows.title: Carl Icahn thought the inflation of 2022 was just like the fall of the Roman Empire. He’s not the only billionaire with ancient Rome on the mind

rows.title: JPMorgan’s Jamie Dimon says Fed may have to hike more because central bank started ‘a day late and a dollar short’ and now is just ‘catching up’

rows.title: Deutsche Bank CEO says Germany risks becoming ‘the sick man of Europe’ unless structural fixes are made: ‘Something urgently needs to change here’

rows.title: Larry Summers says the Fed is ‘considerably too optimistic’ and risks surprises from fast inflation, weak growth—or both

rows.title: This generation of politicians has killed fiscal responsibility–but millennials and Gen Zers will be the ones who pay the price

rows.title: With fewer sellers on the housing market, more scammers are impersonating them

rows.title: 56-year-old cancer patient facing eviction is still on a waiting list for state housing—even though thousands are sitting totally vacant

rows.title: Why the Fed’s dovish stance on interest rates isn’t enough to start popping the champagne corks on inflation

rows.title: How the U.S. job market defied rising interest rates and predictions of high unemployment

rows.title: How many ‘vacant homes’ does China have right now? A former statistics official has an eye-opening prediction

rows.title: Jamie Dimon says Americans are on an economic ‘sugar high’—and he’s urging clients to batten down the hatches and prepare for rates to hit 7%

rows.title: Moving back in with your parents is so common now that it’s nearly lost its stigma

rows.title: The economist who’s been predicting a recession for 18 months says the ‘litmus test’ is finally here, especially with oil headed toward $100 a barrel

rows.title: Deutsche Bank studied 34 past U.S. recessions to identify key warning signs and found that all 4 are flashing red right now

rows.title: Morgan Stanley’s chief investor says the market is stuck in ‘purgatory’ as everyone awaits a recession or rebound in growth

rows.title: Inflation, still a ways off from the Fed’s 2% target, is barely budging as one economist sees a ‘golden path’ developing

rows.title: 5 economic shocks are about to hit the U.S. all at the same time: ‘There are storm clouds out there forming that we’re all seeing and watching—fearfully’

rows.title: Wall Street giant Larry Fink sees 10-year Treasury yield at 5% or higher ‘because of this embedded inflation. This structural inflation is unlike anything’
